name: Add to cart
summary: Buy block on the product page: stock, quantity, "Add to cart" button and delivery time. Optional: a minimum order, an order unit and a second action such as "Request a quote".
use: Product page, below the Variant picker.
avoid: Product cards: one small button is enough there.
anatomy: Quantity stepper, Accent button (fills the space), optional wishlist.
Optional hint below that row, over the full width.
Delivery time with a truck icon.
Optional second action: a secondary button with one line of explanation below it.
figmaProps: Default, Low stock, Out of stock
Out of stock: quantity and button off, delivery time hidden.
Line below the row. Off by default.
Off by default. Change the button text in the nested Button.
The line below the second button.
reactProps: Use these when the page needs the quantity live, for example for a price per quantity. Without them Add to cart keeps the quantity itself.
Default 1 and 10. Give a higher max for bulk orders.
Order unit, default 1. See Quantity stepper.
Line below the quantity and the button, for example "Add 200 more for €0.48 each".
Second, smaller action below the buy button.
One line that says when to choose the second action.
Default 'accent', so the buy action stands out from the brand color.
behaviour: After adding, the Mini cart usually opens (see Examples).
With a minimum order the quantity starts at that minimum.
The hint, and the message after a corrected quantity, sit below the whole row. The stepper and the buttons stay in place.
While one action is busy, the other does not respond, so nothing is sent twice.
When sold out the second action stays available.
a11y: Announce that the item was added (Mini cart or a status message), not only visually.
The explanation is the description of the second button, so a screen reader reads it with the button.
A busy button keeps the focus and says it is busy (aria-busy).
content: Button: "Add to cart". Sold out: "Sold out".
Second action: say what you get and when. "For large orders or a custom print. You get a price within one working day."
do: Keep one main action. The second action is always the smaller one.
dont: A disabled button with no explanation why.
A second action without a line that says how it differs from buying.
open: "Email me when it is back in stock" does not exist yet.
Assumption: when sold out the second action stays available, because asking for a quote can still make sense. Hide it yourself if it does not.
Assumption: the second action sits on its own row, left, at its own width, so it does not compete with the buy button.
maxQuantity stays 10 by default. A shop for bulk orders has to set it on every product page.
